start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 3 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)` and, for the 8th trick, another 3. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 3 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

start.README.md:
# Barnacle A trick-taking card game for three players with a rotating trump suit. The engine is headless: a `Game` created from a seed, a list of legal commands and exact text for every reply. ## Deck and deal 24 cards: ranks `9 T J Q K A` (in this order, `9` lowest) in the suits `C D H S`. A card is written rank then suit: `9C`, `TD`, `AS`. The deck starts in this order: all clubs from `9` to `A`, then diamonds, hearts, spades (`9C TC JC QC KC AC 9D ... AS`). Randomness: `state = seed mod 2^31`; `next()` sets `state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) mod 2^31` and returns the new state. The deck is shuffled by Fisher-Yates from the end: for `i` from 23 down to 1: `j = (next() >> 16) mod (i + 1)`, swap the cards at positions `i` and `j`. Then the card at position `k` goes to player `k mod 3` (three players `P0`, `P1`, `P2`; 8 cards each). A hand is kept sorted by suit (`C D H S`) and, inside a suit, by rank ascending. Nothing else uses the generator. ## Play There are 8 tricks, numbered from 1. `P0` leads trick 1; the winner of a trick leads the next one. In a trick the players play one card each, in turn order starting with the leader (`P0 P1 P2` wrap around). A player must *follow suit*: if the hand holds at least one card of the led suit (the suit of the first card of the trick) only those cards may be played; otherwise any card. The trump suit changes with the trick number: trick 1 `C`, trick 2 `D`, trick 3 `H`, trick 4 `S`, trick 5 `C` again, and so on (`SUITS[(trick - 1) mod 4]`). Commands are exact strings `play ` (for example `play QH`). `legal_moves()` lists the `play` commands the player to move may use (in any order; empty when the game is over). Anything else is illegal. ### Winning a trick When the third card is played the trick is decided at once. If any card of the trick has the trump suit of this trick, the highest trump wins; otherwise the highest card *of the led suit* wins (cards of other suits never win). The winner scores `1 + 2 * (number of jacks in the trick)`. After trick 8 the game is over: the player with the most points wins; if two or three players share the top score the game is a draw. ### Events returned by `apply` `P

plays `; when the card completes a trick `; trick won by P +` follows; after trick 8 `; game over: P wins` or `; game over: draw` is appended too. ## API (crate `barnacle`, `src/lib.rs`) ```rust use barnacle::Game; let mut g = Game::new(seed); // seed: u32 g.legal_moves() -> Vec g.apply(cmd: &str) -> Result // Ok(events), or Err(message) and no change for an illegal command g.scores() -> [u32; 3] g.is_over() -> bool g.render() -> String ``` ### `render()` Lines joined by `\n` (no trailing newline): `trick /8 trump to play P` (after the last trick: `over after 8 tricks`); one line per player `P

: ` (`P

: ` with nothing after it when the hand is empty); `table: ` followed by the cards of the trick in play as `P

=` separated by spaces, or `table: -` when the table is empty; `scores: `. Example at the start of a game with seed 1: ``` trick 1/8 trump C to play P0 P0: QC KC TH QH KH TS JS KS P1: AC TD JD QD AD 9H QS AS P2: 9C TC JC 9D KD JH AH 9S table: - scores: 0 0 0 ``` ## Tests `cargo test --offline --quiet` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter/mod.rs` shows how the API is called; the format is described at the top of `tests/scenarios.rs`).

prompt: Handing this one over. The Barnacle engine (`src/lib.rs`) has a defect that a player noticed: Three separate problems. First: The deals don't match the README's reference shuffle for a given seed: the swap partner of a card is drawn from a range one card too small. Second: After a trick the player who won it doesn't necessarily lead the next one: the lead seems to go back to the first player. Third: A trump card played on a trick does not win it if somebody played a higher card of the led suit. I couldn't spot it by reading the rules code. The spec is README.md.
